executable_actions.on_failure: Keep Stage7 closure blocked. Do not run boundary tracing, single-layer simulation, board-wrapper simulation, or modify DUT/reference/tolerance artifacts. Return the unresolved loader token or dependency-selection mismatch for another bounded checker-contract repair.
executable_actions.rationale: Repair the earliest violated verification contract by aligning artifact loading and dependency filtering with the active operator-leaf closure. This is a checker/harness repair, not a DUT repair, and it must preserve all mandatory semantic checks.

executable_actions.on_failure: If any mandatory token or hash remains unresolved, classify it as a checker/harness artifact-binding defect and return to the preceding bounded repair. If real evidence contradicts a reported leaf pass, record the exact contradicted artifact or gate before requesting a targeted backtrack. Do not promote to single-layer execution and do not run board tools.
executable_actions.rationale: Validate the refined current-layer contract against the existing immutable real-tool bundle. The rerun must prove that mandatory semantic artifacts are actually bound while later-layer prerequisites remain pending.

observations: All eight operator-leaf required gates are reported pass, including the target-model reference, semantic testbench, leaf functional and golden comparisons, complete real-weight artifacts, and operator-leaf semantic aggregate.
The single-transformer-layer gates are pending_later_stage rather than failed. Board AXI/DDR and runtime gates are also pending_later_stage and remain blocked by hierarchy.

No failing hardware transaction, failed CCTG boundary, observed-versus-expected value, root candidate module, or contradicting lower-layer trace is supplied. Therefore an RTL or interconnect repair is not justified.

The earliest violated contract is the Stage7 checker/harness contract: it must load the mandatory current-scope semantic tokens from the existing immutable artifacts while excluding later-layer dependencies from the operator-leaf closure decision.

The generated repair_step.00 is illegal for the current ambiguity because its resolved protocol is an all-target-layer, exact-board-wrapper simulator and its own tool-scope check says it cannot provide a single-layer trace rerun.

The authoritative sacg_memory_truth contains no active contamination barriers and no open retry or backtrack requests. Historical text in the verifier summary claiming such blockers must not be treated as current SACG-memory state.
The supplied evidence does not authorize changing the model, shapes, numeric tolerance, data order, weight layout, runtime ABI, RTL, or board wrapper.
proposed_actions: Supersede repair_step.00 with a bounded Stage7 checker/gate-scope repair; do not invoke case_vcs_functional_sim or any single-layer/board tool.
Bind the operator-leaf precondition loader to the existing target-model reference manifest, complete DUT weight-binding manifest, semantic-testbench manifest, and numeric-policy hash.
Filter the closure dependency set by the active operator_leaf_closure level so later single-layer, multilayer, AXI/DDR, and board-runtime gates remain pending rather than failing.

Rerun only case_functional_sim_precondition_check and verification_agent_decision_check through the grounded targeted failed-checker path, while auditing immutable artifact hashes and required real-tool evidence.
Promote the operator-leaf closure only if the repaired checker passes without suppressing mandatory semantic evidence. Single-layer execution becomes eligible only after that promotion.
risks: Merely deleting the three missing-token checks would create a false pass. The repaired checker must resolve `target_model_inference`, `dut_weight_binding`, and `numeric_policy_sha256` to the already-produced immutable artifacts and validate their hashes and scope.
Allowing pending single-layer or board prerequisites to remain in the operator-leaf dependency set can cause repeated false closure failures and out-of-order board simulation.

Executing the proposed board-wrapper simulator now could contaminate localization by mixing single-layer, multilayer, AXI/DDR, runtime, and exact-wrapper behavior before the current closure is accepted.

Regenerating reference outputs, stimulus, tolerances, testbench semantics, or weight manifests during this repair could invalidate otherwise reusable leaf evidence or conceal an artifact-loader defect.

A later contradiction in model configuration, tensor shapes, numeric policy, stream/data order, memory layout, runtime ABI, implementation hierarchy, or exact board-wrapper hashes must be routed to its owning layer; none is presently evidenced as a current blocker.

constraints: Later single-layer, multilayer, AXI/DDR, and board-runtime gates that are pending later scope must not fail an operator_leaf_closure run.
Current-scope semantic preconditions must still bind target-model inference, complete DUT weight-consumption evidence, and the numeric-policy hash; they must not be waived to repair gate scope.
Do not reopen passed operator-leaf modules without a boundary trace or contract change that contradicts their pass evidence.
Do not run single-layer or board-wrapper tools before the operator-leaf closure artifact is cleanly accepted.
Checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy and tolerance, semantic testbench contract, and board-wrapper hashes remain immutable.
Transformer-block scope excludes embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, and sampling.
edges: operator_leaf_modules pass evidence -> Stage7 operator-leaf closure decision

output.summary: The earliest visible violation is the Stage7 verification precondition/gate-scope contract, not a Transformer RTL boundary. The operator-leaf layer has pass evidence for every required gate, while single-layer and board AXI/DDR gates are explicitly pending later scope. The failing precondition both fails to bind the existing mandatory leaf semantic artifacts (`target_model_inference`, `dut_weight_binding`, and `numeric_policy_sha256`) and incorrectly treats later-layer prerequisites as current blockers. The smallest legal repair is to correct that checker artifact-loading and active-layer filtering, then rerun only the failed Stage7 closure checkers. The proposed single-layer boundary-trace run through an all-layer board-wrapper simulator is out of order and must not execute.
